pr_title: kernel: mmu: Fix static analysis issue
pr_body:
Instead of performing a set of relative address comparisons using pointers of type 'uint8_t *', we leverage the existing IN_RANGE() macro and perform the comparisons using 'uintptr_t'.

Fixes #65375

issue_context.body:

comments:
The claim in Coverity is that 

```
Inequality comparison against NULL (BAD_COMPARE)
null_misuse: Comparing pointer dest_addr against NULL using anything besides == or != is likely to be incorrect.

```

Although I think that this specific issue is a false positive, further analysis of the code does identify three other suspect items in that code block.

1. `(dest_addr < Z_VIRT_RAM_END)` [on line 781](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/kernel/mmu.c#L781) contains a potential off by 1 type error. As Z_VIRT_RAM_END = (Z_VIRT_RAM_START + Z_VIRT_RAM_SIZE), an unfortunate selection of values could result in that evaluating to 0.
2. There is a separate concern about `(dest_addr + aligned_size) >= Z_VIRT_RAM_START)` [on line 782](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/kernel/mmu.c#L782) that the compiler may omit this check as it may assume that increasing the pointer will not result in a wrap-around condition and it will re-use the result from [line 780](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/kernel/mmu.c#L780)
3. [Line 783](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/kernel/mmu.c#L783) is a repeat of the issue on [line 781](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/kernel/mmu.c#L781)
Marked the Coverity issue as a false positive. The other items that I identified are distinct from this issue and will be tracked via a separate issue.

review_comments: I think you can skip the minus 1 here, as you have remove 1 byte from the end value. Or else the comparison would be off by 1 byte.

I think that it is needed. The _IN_RANGE()_ macro uses a _<=_ comparison for the upper bound and _Z_VIRT_RAM_END_ is simply "start address + size". Furthermore, in the corner case where that would take us to the very end of the addresses, without the "-1", our end address would wrap around to zero. With the "-1", we ensure that we remain within the boundaries.
